title: Iced Bottled Black Decaffeinated Diet Tea

content.title: About
content.content: Iced black decaffeinated diet tea in a bottle is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from selected black tea leaves that have undergone a decaffeination process. The drink is sweetened with artificial sweeteners, making it low‑calorie, and sealed in a hermetic glass or plastic bottle.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually performed by water‑extraction or CO₂ methods, preserving the tea’s flavor profile.
Black tea retains polyphenols even after the caffeine is removed.
Iced tea is a popular summer refreshment because it quickly quenches thirst.
Diet versions use sucralose or stevia instead of sugar, reducing calories to 0–5 kcal per 100 ml.
Bottle packaging protects the drink from light and oxygen, extending shelf life.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Polyphenols in black tea help neutralize free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Regular consumption of black tea has been linked to modest reductions in blood pressure.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Tannins stimulate gastric juice secretion, aiding the digestion of meals.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: The diet version contains virtually no calories, making it suitable for weight‑control diets.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Iced tea provides fluid intake, especially useful in hot weather.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some people are sensitive to sucralose or other sweeteners, which can cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Tannins may affect the absorption of certain drugs, such as iron supplements.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: A modest amount of salt is sometimes added for flavor; those with hypertension should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chill the bottle, open, and drink straight. The tea can also serve as a base for cocktails, or be garnished with a slice of lemon or fresh mint for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.
